articles.title: Tested: 21+ Best Body Lotions for Dry Skin | NBC Selected
articles.summary: These expert-recommended moisturizers can help your skin stay hydrated and healthy. Shop the best body lotions for dry skin from brands like CeraVe, La Roche-Posay and more.
articles.body: The benefits of an effective lotion extend beyond its ability to soften your skin: It should also help lock in moisture and support the skin barrier, says board-certified dermatologist Dr. Hadley King. “An impaired barrier will leave the skin more vulnerable to damage, dryness, irritation, inflammation and infection,” she says. I spoke to dermatologists about the importance of moisturizing, what to look for in a quality body lotion (including ingredients) and which lotions you should use based on your skin type. I also gathered some expert-recommended lotions to consider, as well as options NBC Selected staffers have tried and loved. Want more from NBC Selected? Sign up for our newsletter, The Selection, and shop smarter. The best body lotions for dry skin With this expert guidance in mind, I rounded up a handful of dermatologist-recommended lotions and creams, plus ones NBC Selected staff have tried, to help your dry skin heal. Best overall This NBC Selected Wellness Award winner, which is formulated with hyaluronic acid and ceramides to heal dry skin, comes recommended by Dr. Shoshana Marmon, a board-certified dermatologist and assistant professor at New York Medical College. Former NBC Selected managing editor Leah Ginsberg also swears by it: “The two things I love most are its soft texture and I notice more of a moisturizing effect on my skin that lasts longer compared to other creams I’ve used and definitely more than when I use lotions,” she says. Ginsberg also appreciates that it doesn’t have a strong scent or a hefty price tag. Best for skin barrier repair “I’ve been using La Roche-Posay products for years and love their gentle scent and the fact that they’re lightweight, providing deep moisture without leaving behind a greasy residue,” says former NBC Selected editor Christina Colizza. The moisturizer is also a favorite of Marmon’s because it is formulated with ceramides, shea butter, glycerin and niacinamide. Best for very dry skin This highly rated body lotion helps keep skin moisturized for up to 48 hours, according to the brand. The formula relies on ceramides, an emollient our experts recommend, to hydrate the skin and prevent dryness. Eucerin’s Advanced Repair Body Lotion is also fragrance-free. Best cream Although this NBC Selected Wellness Award winner has a thicker consistency than your typical lotion, it leaves skin soft and hydrated without feeling heavy or greasy, in our experience. “The hydration I got from the lotion lasted all day, and I didn’t feel like I needed to reapply it all the time,” says former NBC Page Alexa Casanueva. Suitable for all skin types, this noncomedogenic moisturizer also has a subtle coconut scent. Best long-lasting “This lotion makes my skin really soft after using it. With most body creams, I end up having to wash my hands after applying because of the greasy, sticky feeling it leaves on my skin, but this is not the case with Hempz,” says NBC Selected editorial operations associate Jem Alabi. “The scent is really nice and natural, and it lasts for a long time.” It has hemp seed oil and shea butter to provide up to 48 hours of hydration, according to the brand. Best for eczema Vanicream is by no means a new, splashy brand, but it’s a stalwart in the world of skin and hair care and comes recommended by Marmon. Out of all my body lotions, this one stands out because it gives me more moisture than any of the other ones I’ve tried and doesn’t cause any eczema flare-ups. In fact, it actually helps treat my eczema and soothes any itchy, dry, red patches. If you prefer a thicker consistency, consider the cream version, which I also use daily, if not weekly. Best exfoliating Marmon also recommends Amlactin’s moisturizer for dry skin. It’s formulated without parabens or fragrances and relies on humectants like glycerin to hydrate the skin. Also, the lotion contains 12% lactic acid, which the brand says is both a powerful humectant and gentle exfoliant that can relieve skin issues like keratosis pilaris. Best for sensitive skin King also recommends this option from Vaseline, which contains humectants (like glycerin) to hydrate the skin, emollients( like shea butter and sunflower seed oil) to support the skin barrier and occlusives (like petrolatum) to lock in moisture. It’s formula also includes colloidal oatmeal, which helps to soothe and protect the skin, she says. Best multitasking lotion This body lotion combines key hydrating ingredients like shea butter to help improve tone and texture and protect and moisturize the skin, according to the brand. It’s the perfect all-in-one cream, in my opinion. I see and feel a difference in how my skin looks, but I also love how fast-absorbing it is, and despite its lightweight feel, I feel like my skin is hydrated from morning to night. Best fragrance-free When it comes to treating her itchy, dry, and sensitive skin, NBC Selected reporter Zoe Malin reaches for this lotion. “I apply this hydrating cream whenever I start to feel uncomfortable, and it soothes my skin,” she says. “The skin on my legs tends to get dry and cracked in the winter, and if I use this before I go to bed, it’s significantly more moisturized in the morning.” Editor’s pick Made for dry or sensitive skin or those who live in colder areas and need intense moisture, this cream uses ingredients like squalane and ceramides to repair and strengthen the skin barrier and hydrate and lock in moisture, according to the brand. My skin feels more comfortable and less tight, appears way less dry, and any cracks I have are reduced overnight. I cannot recommend this body moisturizer enough. Best splurge This is a body butter you don’t have to stop using in the summer because it’s nourishing without being heavy or greasy, says NBC Selected senior editor Nikki Brown. The moisturizer focuses on improving dry and damaged skin and increasing firmness and tightness, according to the brand. “A little goes a long way, which is always nice when you don’t want to sacrifice a huge chunk of money for quality products,” says Brown. Best for acne-prone skin Former NBC Selected reporter Harry Rabinowitz is a fan of Cetaphil’s lotion as both a body and face moisturizer. “It’s totally unscented, it comes in a large, affordable bottle, and I’ve seen it recommended by many dermatologists,” he says. Cetaphil is formulated with hydrating glycerin and is noncomedogenic, meaning it shouldn’t clog pores or cause breakouts. Best packaging It took me forever to find a moisturizer that worked for everyone in my family until I tried this one. My younger brothers (both under the age of 10) swear lotions make them itchy and their skin uncomfortable, but this is the first one they haven’t complained about and don’t mind applying. It’s not too thick or thin, has a subtle scent that doesn’t cause any irritation on all our skin types and is super fast absorbing. Best firming This moisturizing, eucalyptus-scented body lotion has five peptides in its formula to help regulate cellular activity for improved skin health. These peptides also focus on firming and strengthening the skin, according to the brand. “This body cream’s eucalyptus scent is present but not overpowering, and it reminds me of the cream a spa would use for an aromatherapy massage,” says Malin, who is cautious about fragrances in her lotion because she has sensitive skin. “I apply it post-shower to lock moisture into my skin, and while it takes a little blending to fully absorb, it’s lightweight and doesn’t leave behind a greasy residue.” This lotion is available in three additional fragrances (Santal, Olibanum and Hinoki) and a fragrance-free option, which has the National Eczema Association’s Seal of Acceptance. Best for dry, cracked skin This Curél body lotion is fragrance-free and specifically targets extra dry, tight skin, according to the brand. It has hydrating ingredients like ceramides, shea butter and oatmeal that lock in moisture for up to 24 hours, according to the brand. Best non-greasy lotion This Summer Fridays body lotion, another NBC Selected Wellness Award winner, combines humectants, emollients and occlusives like hyaluronic acid, ceramides, glycerin and natural oils to hydrate and soften the skin, according to the brand. The lotion, which has a coconut, vanilla and almond scent, is in constant rotation for former NBC page Mikhaila Archer because it has a great texture that doesn’t feel too thin or thick on her skin, she says. Most lightweight Former NBC Page Hannah Fuechtman reaches for Illiyoon’s Ceramide Ato Lotion to moisturize her dry skin during the winter. “I have incredibly dry skin, especially when the cold weather hits, and this is one of the only lotions that protects my skin,” she says. “I love how this lightweight, fragrance-free formula goes on smoothly and doesn’t leave my skin feeling sticky.” Illiyoon has products specifically for sensitive skin, so it’s a great pick if you fall into that skin type, too, says Fuechtman. Best retinol lotion This body lotion uses an encapsulated retinol complex to improve skin texture, tone and firmness, according to the brand. The silky, fast-absorbing formula also reduces irritation and redness while providing overall moisture and hydration, according to Naturium. The lotion is available in a larger version with pump packaging and is also sold in a bundle. Best ointment Not quite a lotion, not quite a cream, but deserving of an honorable mention from Marmon is Aquaphor’s healing ointment. The balm won’t spread across your skin like the other recommendations on this list, but it’s great for spot treating rough patches on your skin and other itchy spots. It also ranks in NBC Selected’s guides on how to heal dry, chapped lips and the best hand creams to heal dry skin. Best scented Though you should proceed with caution when it comes to heavily-fragranced moisturizers, King uses this Eos lotion and says she’s very happy with it. Plus, it’s packed with humectants, emollients and occlusives like shea butter, glycerin, cocoa seed butter and petrolatum, she says. Best in-shower lotion This in-shower body moisturizer is another favorite of Brown, who tested it for our NBC Selected Wellness Awards and has repurchased multiple times since. “The application process takes some getting used to because you don’t rub it off — you just let it sit there and allow the shower water to run over,” says Brown. “I love using this after swimming laps when I’m tired and want to just get everything done in the shower. And I’ve gotten many compliments on how soft my skin feels.” Best for face and body “I finished a bottle of this moisturizer and quickly bought another because of how pleased I was with it,” says Alabi. “I have very dry skin and wanted to actively treat the scarring and keratosis pilaris on my legs. This lotion made my skin very soft during the winter and definitely brightened up my legs and arms. I even felt comfortable using this on my face, which simplified my skin care routine greatly. The scent is light and pleasant and genuinely feels nice going on the skin compared to other retinol body products I’ve tried. If you are consistent with use, you’ll notice a fabulous difference in your skin health.” How I picked the best body lotions for dry skin When shopping for a body lotion, our experts recommend considering the following factors, all of which I kept in mind to pull together the above list: Ingredients: Look for humectants like hyaluronic acid that attract water from the environment to hydrate the skin. Emollients like ceramides improve the skin’s texture, while occlusives like petrolatum hold onto moisture and prevent skin from drying out, according to our experts. Skin type: Consider a body lotion that fits your specific skin type. If you have very dry skin, look for rich creams that are formulated with more hydrating oils, experts say. If you have sensitive skin, you should avoid fragrances and other potential irritants like dyes, while those with oily and acne-prone skin should consider lightweight, noncomedogenic moisturizers.Price: While there are nice lotions that are on the pricier side, many of the ones below are available for less than $20. How to shop for body lotion for dry skin “Moisturizer is a catch-all term for something that hydrates the skin,” says Marmon. Whether a product is sold as a lotion, cream, body butter or a similar product (more on what distinguishes each below), they should contain humectants to hydrate the skin, emollients to support the skin barrier and occlusives to lock in moisture, says King. Some lotions also have additional ingredients for specific concerns, like lactic acid to gently exfoliate rough or bumpy skin, or retinol to reduce fine lines and wrinkles, she says. Humectants: “Humectants like hyaluronic acid, glycerin and urea attract water from the environment to increase moisture in the skin,” says Marmon. “They need to be used along with the other components in order to retain the water content,” says King.Emollients: Emollients “help in skin barrier function, membrane fluidity and cell signaling leading to overall improvement in skin texture and appearance,” says King. They soothe the skin, filling in any gaps and cracks. Some examples of emollients in moisturizers include squalene, shea butter, fatty acids and ceramides.Occlusives: “Occlusives are oils and waxes which form an inert layer on the skin and physically block transepidermal water loss,” says King, meaning they enable the skin to hold onto moisture. Examples include petrolatum (the main ingredient in Vaseline, or Aquaphor, for example), beeswax, mineral oil, silicones, lanolin and zinc oxide. “Balms and ointments are commonly occlusive,” says Marmon. Meet our dermatology experts At NBC Selected, we work with experts who have specialized knowledge and authority based on relevant training and/or experience. We also take steps to ensure all expert advice and recommendations are made independently and without undisclosed financial conflicts of interest. Dr. Hadley King is a board-certified dermatologist in New York City. Dr. Shoshana Marmon is a board-certified dermatologist in Brooklyn, New York and Assistant Professor at New York Medical College. Why trust NBC Selected? Bianca Alvarez is a former associate reporter at NBC Selected. For this story, she interviewed dermatologists and gathered their recommendations. She also compiled a list of NBC Selected staff favorites and researched highly rated body lotions that met expert guidance. articles.title: Why Kids Are Saying ‘Gyat’—and What Parents Should Know About the Slang Term
articles.summary: You’ve probably heard your teen throwing the term gyatt around. But what does it mean? And should you let your kid say it?
articles.body:
The term "gyat" has roots in African American Vernacular English (AAVE) but has been misused and distorted in modern slang, especially by middle schoolers.

Kids often use "gyat" to comment on bodies, creating unsafe or uncomfortable environments, particularly for girls and marginalized groups.

Teaching children about the origins and implications of words like "gyat" can help them use language more thoughtfully and respectfully.

The term "gyat" has roots in African American Vernacular English (AAVE) but has been misused and distorted in modern slang.

Kids often use "gyat" to comment on bodies, which can create unsafe or uncomfortable environments, especially for girls and marginalized groups.

Gyatt or gyat is a term that has been around for centuries, eventually showing up in online spaces in the early aughts. More recently, the term has been spread via popular internet culture and infiltrated middle schools everywhere. The current adaptation of the term gyat refers to the shape of someone's body or—plainly—a big butt. Gyat is commonly used in comment sections of videos or as body commentary in schools. Middle-schoolers will use gyat as a noun, using variations, such as "Level One Gyatt," "Negative Gyat," and "Sticking out your gyatt."

Others might say that gyat or gyatt is an acronym for a variety of different words. Kids report telling their teachers and parents that gyat stands for "girl, you ate that" or "get your act together." However, other, more inappropriate acronyms like "girl, your a** thick" have surfaced. Below, we take a closer look at the term, its history, and what you need to know as a parent.

Although middle schoolers are using gyat to make inappropriate remarks on people's bodies, the word has a history that stems from African American Vernacular English (AAVE) . Gyat has historically been a way to spell out, phonetically transcribe, or represent a specific pronunciation of god or god damn.

The word gyatt first appeared in AAVE as early as the 1700s and has origins in the Black Southern and Jamaican African diaspora. When enslaved people from all over the Caribbean and Africa came to the United States, they were not given a means to communicate with one another and were denied from learning Standard American English (SAE). As a result, they had to teach themselves how to communicate by ear and a dialect formed called AAVE.

AAVE makes use of liaisons, in which the beginning of one word gets connected to the end of another, consonants can get blended and words with similar vowel sounds get merged together. AAVE, like any other dialect, has grammatical rules that guide its usage, many of which are ignored by people who attempt to adopt the dialect. Many terms commonly known as internet slang have origins in AAVE and have been used for decades. Terms like "cap," "periodt," and "camp" all have historically been associated with AAVE, and have been convoluted to have distorted—often unrecognizable—meanings.

Such is the case with the current usage of the word gyatt, which initially was used as an expression of excitement or surprise by the African American community. But how did a word that originated hundreds of years ago get turned into a term your middle-schooler mutters between giggles to their friends?

Teens and tweens have adopted and repurposed the term gyatt to mean a big butt. They use the term as a noun and often in response to someone's body. It's typical for kids to litter comment sections of a TikTok with phrases like "Negative Gyat" or "Level 100 gyat" or "I Gyat to See That." It's also been reported that kids are using gyat to comment on teacher's bodies. One person tweeted, "My aunt is a teacher and apparently her students say 'gyatt' every time she bends over."

Gyat is pronounced like the word "Fiat" with a "G" in front, or like geey-yah-tuh.

According to Dictionary.com, gyat refers to someone with a curvaceous body, while gyatt describes a person with a large butt. However, both spellings are used to generally describe a large butt.

Gyat really means "god" as in "god damn." It is commonly used to express excitement, surprise, or admiration. Interestingly, the original meaning of the term also has controversial usage. Though gyat means "god" as in "god damn," it is typically used in the context of making a public remark on someone's body (similar to terms like "big back" ), which is how it eventually was convoluted to its current usage.

How Gyat Became a Part of Your Kids' Language

Simply put, gyat became a part of your kids language through the internet. Social media platforms like Twitch and TikTok popularized this term among Generation Alpha, and the term boasts 6.5 billion views on TikTok. Gyat was introduced online by various Twitch streamers (similar to Gen Alpha slang term fanum tax ), including YourRage who first coined the current usage of gyat and KaiCenet who popularized it. When Kai Cenet popularized the term to his over 10 million Twitch followers, which skew on the younger side in comparison to other streamers, it quickly became a funny and cool way to respond to his streams and suddenly gyat was everywhere—even in schools.

But should a word that has been semantically shifted to represent an oversexualized body part be a part of your child's vocabulary? Some people argue that the term is simply an innocent TikTok phrase, but it could represent a harrowing future and disproportionately impact young girls, overweight children, and Black/Latinx students. And historically, this group has been oversexualized and unprotected. The current usage of the word gyat, is a form of cat-calling, reducing teens and tweens to their bodies, which creates unsafe spaces for them.

Cat-calling or making public remarks on someone's body can lead to dangerous situations. In Chicago, a 19-year-old woman was tragically murdered by a man whose cat calls she ignored. It's a verbal form of sexual harassment and makes people feel uncomfortable and unsafe. Though gyat can be used outside of this context, it's important to note that this is the most common context of the current usage of gyat.

The semantic shift of the word gyat represents a longstanding and complicated tradition with AAVE. The appropriation of the term is another example of how people do not respect or acknowledge the validity of the dialect and the grammar that rules it. Just like any dialect, AAVE has grammar rules that dictate how the language should be used.

According to British linguist Geoffrey K. Pullum , "The majority of English speakers think AAVE is just English with two added factors: some special slang terms and a lot of grammatical mistakes. They are simply wrong about this." It's important to note that Black people have historically been discriminated against for the use of AAVE; for example, standardized tests were considered to not be inclusive due to marking down students who use AAVE in their essays.

AAVE is a dialect studied in universities and colleges around the world and people who grew up speaking in AAVE, can tell when it's being used incorrectly. This issue even ripples into many marketing campaigns as big corporations increasingly use AAVE to sell products and appeal to an unassuming audience. Meanwhile, the creators of the dialect—the Black community, especially the Black queer community—continue to suffer discrimination when using their own dialect. As a result, words that are simply a part of Black culture become meme-fied and appropriated.

Words like gyat and other AAVE terms are not internet slang, they have an important history, and kids should know the origins of the words they adopt—perhaps knowing the history would make a difference on if they chose to use it.

articles.title: Simpósio na UENF discute saúde mental e desafios do ambiente acadêmico | G1
articles.standfirst: Evento reuniu estudantes, professores, pesquisadores e técnicos em Campos para debater sofrimento psíquico, relações dentro da universidade e novas questões trazidas pela inteligência artificial.
articles.summary: Evento reuniu estudantes, professores, pesquisadores e técnicos em Campos para debater sofrimento psíquico, relações dentro da universidade e novas questões trazidas pela IA.
articles.body:
A Universidade Estadual do Norte Fluminense Darcy Ribeiro ( UENF ), em Campos dos Goytacazes , no Norte Flumineses, realizou nos dias 9 e 10 de setembro, o IV Simpósio de Saúde Mental do Norte-Noroeste Fluminense.

O evento reuniu estudantes, professores, pesquisadores e técnicos para discutir os desafios relacionados à saúde mental dentro e fora do ambiente universitário.

Com o tema “Universidade e Saúde Mental: Desafios, Reflexões e Contemporaneidade”, a programação contou com palestras, mesas-redondas, rodas de conversa, grupos de trabalho e atividades artísticas.

A proposta foi ampliar o debate sobre os fatores que podem contribuir para o sofrimento psíquico e refletir sobre as relações e as formas de produção dentro da própria universidade.

Segundo a professora Verusca Reis, do Programa de Pós-graduação em Cognição e Linguagem da UENF e uma das organizadoras do evento, era necessário analisar se a maneira como as pessoas trabalham e se relacionam também pode contribuir para processos de adoecimento.

“A ideia é que a gente compreenda o sofrimento psíquico que a gente vem passando, não somente na sociedade, mas também dentro da universidade. Se tem a forma como nós produzimos, como nós nos relacionamos, se isso também gera adoecimento”, explica Verusca.

Além das questões diretamente relacionadas à rotina acadêmica, o simpósio abordou transformações que fazem parte da realidade atual das universidades. Entre elas esteve o avanço da inteligência artificial e os impactos do uso dessas ferramentas por estudantes e professores.

A presença cada vez maior da tecnologia no cotidiano acadêmico também levanta discussões sobre limites, responsabilidade e os efeitos que essas mudanças podem provocar na formação e nas relações dentro das instituições de ensino.

Para Davis Lichote, aluno de pós-graduação em nível de doutorado e também organizador do simpósio, falar sobre saúde mental é especialmente importante diante da realidade vivida atualmente nas universidades.

“Falar sobre saúde mental nesse momento que a gente vive na vida, dentro da realidade principalmente da universidade, é algo muito importante pensar sobre isso e o simpósio nasceu exatamente com esse objetivo, de poder levar as pessoas a fazer uma reflexão, a pensar o que nós podemos fazer para melhorar a saúde mental dentro da universidade”, afirma.

Davis destacou ainda que a intenção é transformar as discussões em propostas capazes de contribuir para mudanças no ambiente acadêmico.

“Principalmente a partir disso propor ações para que a gente possa melhorar o ambiente acadêmico e assim também fazer com que políticas de saúde mental sejam estabelecidas dentro da universidade”, completa.

A programação buscou aproximar diferentes áreas do conhecimento e experiências relacionadas à saúde mental, criando um espaço para troca de informações e discussão de possíveis estratégias de enfrentamento.

Além de discutir os problemas que afetam estudantes e trabalhadores das universidades, o encontro teve como objetivo estimular a construção de propostas e ações que possam contribuir para um ambiente acadêmico mais saudável.

O IV Simpósio de Saúde Mental do Norte-Noroeste Fluminense foi realizado nos dias 9 e 10 de setembro, na UENF, em Campos dos Goytacazes.

articles.title: Terceira guerra mundial é maior risco global, aponta ONU | G1
articles.standfirst: Possibilidade subiu 16 posições em dois anos e superou mudanças climáticas, pandemias e a disrupção tecnógica devido à IA.
articles.summary: Pesquisa da ONU com 1.300 especialistas aponta guerra em larga escala como maior risco global. A ameaça subiu 16 posições desde 2024.
articles.body:
Sessão no Conselho de Segurança da ONU que votou e rejeitou resolução permitindo uso da força no Estreito de Ormuz, em 7 de abril de 2026. — Foto: Jeenah Moon/ Reuters

A possibilidade de uma nova guerra mundial se tornou a principal preocupação entre especialistas em riscos globais, segundo um relatório da Organização das Nações Unidas ( ONU ) divulgado nesta terça-feira (15). O tema subiu 16 posições em relação a 2024, a maior alta entre os 28 riscos analisados.

A pesquisa ouviu 1.300 pessoas de governos, organizações internacionais, empresas, universidades e organizações da sociedade civil. Os participantes avaliaram ameaças políticas, econômicas, ambientais, sociais e tecnológicas.

Para 36% dos entrevistados, um conflito em larga escala poderia afetar uma parcela significativa da humanidade em até um ano. O porcentual sobe para 76% quando o prazo considerado é de sete anos.

Terceira guerra mundial vai ao topo dos riscos

A guerra foi o único risco a aparecer entre os seis primeiros em todos os critérios avaliados. O estudo considerou a importância de cada ameaça, a proximidade de seus efeitos, a relação com outros riscos e o nível de preparo das instituições para enfrentá-la.

O cenário mudou em relação a 2024. Naquele ano, ameaças ambientais, desinformação e pandemias estavam entre as principais preocupações. Agora, tensões geopolíticas, conlitos e o enfraquecimento do Estado de Direito ocupam posição central.

A mudança aparece em todas as sete regiões analisadas pela ONU. A guerra em larga escala e as tensões geopolíticas estão entre os dez principais riscos em todas elas e entre os cinco primeiros em seis regiões. Há dois anos, os dois riscos estavam entre os cinco primeiros em apenas uma região.

Outras ameaças também ganharam destaque:

Armas de destruição em massa entraram entre os dez principais riscos na Ásia Central e Meridional, na África Subsaariana e na Oceania.

Na Ásia Oriental e no Sudeste Asiático, cresceram as preocupações com uma possível crise financeira global , os efeitos da inteligência artificial e o poder das empresas de tecnologia .

A inteligência artificial aparece como uma preocupação crescente em outras partes do mundo . Riscos ligados à tecnologia entraram entre os dez principais na Europa e na América do Norte. Ao mesmo tempo, o relatório aponta que o sistema multilateral é considerado pouco preparado para lidar com ameaças tecnológicas.

As mudanças climáticas continuam entre os principais riscos. A falta de ação contra o aquecimento global foi apontada como a ameaça mais importante no conjunto da pesquisa. Já pandemias e riscos biológicos deixaram de aparecer entre os dez primeiros em todas as regiões.

O relatório não é uma previsão . Segundo a ONU, ele representa a percepção dos especialistas sobre os riscos atuais. A maioria dos entrevistados considera a cooperação entre governos a medida mais eficaz para prevenir crises. Para 86%, porém, os recursos destinados à redução de riscos são insuficientes.

articles.title: Tarcísio minimiza impacto eleitoral do caso Master e diz que está revendo 'uma série de questões' no contrato com ViaMobilidade | G1
articles.standfirst: Governador defende investigação ampla sobre o caso Master, afirma que punições a concessionárias de serviços públicos esbarram em recursos administrativos e judiciais e promete fortalecer a regulação estadual.
articles.summary: Governador defende investigação ampla sobre o caso Master, afirma que punições a concessionárias de serviços públicos esbarram em recursos administrativos e judiciais e promete fortalecer a regulação estadual.
articles.body:
O governador de São Paulo e candidato à reeleição, Tarcísio de Freitas ( Republicanos ), afirmou nesta terça-feira (15) que não acredita que as investigações relacionadas ao escândalo do Banco Master tenham impacto sobre sua campanha eleitoral.

A declaração foi dada após ser questionado, em entrevista ao SP1, sobre o alcance das investigações, que miram diferentes autoridades, entre elas o senador Flávio Bolsonaro (PL), apoiado por Tarcísio na disputa à Presidência da República.

"Eu acho que não afeta. A gente tem defendido desde o primeiro momento uma investigação ampla. As pessoas precisam ter noção do que está acontecendo", declarou o governador.

Tarcísio de Freitas (Republicanos) com Alan Severiano no estúdio do 'SP1'. — Foto: Globo/ Bob Paulino

Tarcísio também afirmou que o país vive um momento de "exaustão ética" e de descrença da população na política. Segundo ele, é preciso substituir o "corporativismo" para avançar na responsabilização dos envolvidos.

"A gente vê o eleitor até frio, o eleitor descrente, a gente precisa resgatar a crença nas boas políticas públicas, nas boas propostas e não é o que está acontecendo. Eu acho que a gente precisa sair daquela fase do corporativismo, aquela fase do silêncio para ingressar numa fase de transparência, de apuração, de responsabilização", declarou.

Ainda segundo o governador, a transparência sobre o caso tem especial relevância neste período eleitoral.

"Tudo tem que vir à tona para que o eleitor possa tomar as suas decisões e para que a gente possa seguir caminhando na direção correta. Então eu defendo ampla investigação, transparência, que tudo venha à tona e que o eleitor possa saber o que está acontecendo. Tá na hora de passar o Brasil é limpo", disse Tarcísio.

Revisão do contrato da ViaMobilidade e reforço das agências reguladoras

Questionado sobre falhas recorrentes nas linhas de trem operadas pela ViaMobilidade, concessionária responsável pelas linhas 8-Diamante e 9-Esmeralda do sistema metropolitano, Tarcísio afirmou que o governo pretende revisar aspectos do contrato e endurecer a fiscalização sobre a prestação do serviço.

O governador argumentou que parte dos problemas decorre de deficiências históricas na infraestrutura ferroviária, como sistemas antigos de sinalização. Mas reconheceu que persistem falhas consideradas inaceitáveis.

"A gente está revendo uma série de questões no contrato da ViaMobilidade. A gente deve fazer um grande arranjo. Não foi um contrato licitado por nós, a gente já chegou com esse contrato. Isso foi licitado no governo anterior e obviamente cabe a nós agora fazer a regulação", afirmou.

Segundo Tarcísio, o estado continuará cobrando melhorias da concessionária e verificadores independentes passarão a auxiliar na fiscalização do contrato e na aplicação de eventuais sanções.

Tarcísio de Freitas no estúdio do SP1 — Foto: Globo/ Bob Paulino

O governador também rebateu críticas à capacidade de fiscalização da Agência Reguladora de Serviços Públicos do Estado de São Paulo (Arsesp), após ser confrontado com dados que apontam déficit de fiscais e baixo índice de pagamento das multas aplicadas às concessionárias de transporte sobre trilhos.

"Muitas multas não são pagas porque são questionadas administrativamente, inclusive judicialmente. Se você pegar, vai ver um histórico enorme", afirmou o governador, pontuando que o problema não é exclusivo de São Paulo e acontece também em concessões federais.

Tarcísio afirmou que seu governo tem fortalecido a estrutura das agências reguladoras e citou a aprovação de uma nova lei estadual para ampliar a autonomia desses órgãos. Segundo ele, a legislação criou critérios mais rígidos para a escolha de dirigentes e garantiu independência orçamentária e financeira às agências.

"A gente aprovou uma lei que muda a estrutura das agências reguladoras. A gente tem hoje o framework regulatório mais moderno do Brasil. A gente criou critérios muito rígidos para a escolha de dirigentes e deu autonomia para as agências, inclusive a independência orçamentária e financeira", declarou.

De acordo com o governador, a nova estrutura impede o contingenciamento de recursos arrecadados pelas próprias agências com atividades de fiscalização, o que, segundo ele, amplia a capacidade de monitoramento dos contratos de concessão.

Tarcísio também disse que pretende ampliar o uso de verificadores independentes, profissionais externos responsáveis por auxiliar na apuração de falhas e no acompanhamento das concessionárias.

"Vamos ter os verificadores independentes. Isso é fundamental. É um agente externo que vai nos ajudar, com especialistas, a fazer essas apurações e robustecer os processos de apuração de falhas e de aplicação das sanções", afirmou.

O governador acrescentou que o estado realizou e continuará realizando concursos públicos para reforçar o quadro técnico das agências reguladoras. Segundo ele, já foram autorizadas contratações para esses órgãos e novas vagas devem ser abertas futuramente.

articles.title: Piscina é usada sob pontos de goteira e vazamentos em escola | G1
articles.standfirst: Registro foi feito na Emei Prefeito Luis Di Fiori em Itapetininga (SP), nesta segunda-feira (14). Ao g1, a mãe de uma aluna relatou que o problema estrutural da escola não é recente.
articles.summary: Um vídeo gravado na área interna da Emei Prefeito Luis Antonio Di Fiori Fiores Costa, em Itapetininga, mostra o uso de uma piscina de plástico para o controle de goteiras.
articles.body:
Um vídeo gravado na área interna da Escola Municipal de Educação Infantil (Emei) Prefeito Luis Antonio Di Fiori Fiores Costa, localizada na região central de Itapetininga (SP), mostrou o uso de uma piscina de plástico para o controle da água de goteiras e vazamentos no teto da unidade. O registro foi feito nesta segunda-feira (14).

Nas imagens é possível perceber que a piscina foi colocada logo abaixo dos vazamentos, como uma forma de receber a água. Ao redor, pode ser visto que a parede apresenta manchas de infiltração e o piso está molhado.

Para entender melhor a situação estrutural da unidade municipal de ensino, o g1 conversou com a mãe de uma aluna, nesta terça-feira (15). À reportagem, Sirlei da Silva Gouveia, de 42 anos, funcionária pública estadual, relatou detalhes sobre o estado atual do espaço.

“Eu tenho uma filha de quatro anos e ela está na escola há dois anos. Essa situação começou em fevereiro do ano passado, com as chuvas que ocorreram. Ela [a situação] não chega a abranger a sala que a minha [filha] estuda, é afastada. Mas ainda é perigoso”, disse.

Piscina é usada para conter goteiras e vazamentos em escola municipal de Itapetininga — Foto: Marina Nalesso/Arquivo pessoal

Sirlei disse ao g1 que tem conversado com outros responsáveis pelos alunos sobre a situação, mas que ainda não encaminhou uma reclamação à prefeitura. Desde que sua filha começou a frequentar a unidade, ela começou a participar do conselho da escola.

“É um descaso enorme da prefeitura com as escolas. Isso [o problema] já é recorrente. A escola vai até os seis anos e tem bebês do berçário que também estão lá”, contou.

Sirlei descreve um sentimento de "revolta". "Além de ser mãe, eu sou membro do conselho da escola. A gente acompanha o que acontece lá. A diretora já tomou providências desde o acontecido e não tem retorno. A gente se sente de mãos atadas”, completou.

Apesar da situação atual, a mãe afirmou à reportagem que não irá retirar sua filha da Emei.

“Embora seja perigoso, eu sei que a equipe é competente. Eles cuidam muito bem das crianças. Eles não vão deixar a criança perto da piscina”, relatou.

Imagens feitas pela vereadora de Itapetininga mostra a situação da escola na região central — Foto: Marina Nalesso/Arquivo pessoal

As imagens foram registradas pela vereadora Marina Nalesso Mariano ( PL ) e compartilhadas nas redes sociais nesta segunda-feira (14). Na publicação, a parlamentar apontou que foi acionada por mães de alunos relatando os problemas com as diversas goteiras e infiltrações.

Ao visitar o espaço, a vereadora constatou a situação e apontou que o problema gerou transtornos à comunidade escolar. Ainda no Instagram, Marina apontou que encaminhou a demanda à Secretaria de Educação Municipal.

Em nota ao g1 , a Prefeitura de Itapetininga, por meio da Secretaria de Educação, informou que após as fortes chuvas dos últimos dias, foi constatado que várias telhas se quebraram. Por conta disso, os serviços de manutenção foram iniciados de forma imediata.

articles.title: Apple bundles TV, Arcade with iCloud+; ends standalone Apple One subscriptions in India
articles.summary: Tech News News: Apple is reshaping its subscription business in India. Starting this month, iCloud+ subscribers will get Apple TV and Apple Arcade at no additional co.
articles.body: Apple is reshaping its subscription business in India. Starting this month, iCloud+ subscribers will get Apple TV and Apple Arcade at no additional cost, combining cloud storage, video streaming and gaming in a single subscription.Apple is also introducing Apple Select, a new service integrated into the existing Apple Music app, exclusively for iCloud+ subscribers. This addition extends the expanded bundle’s benefits to the music app, offering subscribers an exclusive collection of music.The expanded service will start at Rs 75 a month for 50GB of storage, with higher storage tiers also available. Subscribers can share the package with up to five family members. The rollout will take place through September.The change will end standalone Apple TV and Apple Arcade subscriptions sold directly by Apple in India. Existing individual subscriptions will be cancelled, with users continuing to access the services through iCloud+. Apple said access would remain uninterrupted and Arcade game progress and saves would be preserved.Apple One, which bundles several Apple services, will also close to new subscribers in India. Existing subscribers will retain their subscriptions. This means new customers seeking Apple’s combined storage and entertainment offering will be directed towards iCloud+, while current Apple One users can continue with their existing package.Apple One currently has two plans in India: Individual at Rs 195 a month, with 50GB of iCloud+ storage, and Family at Rs 365 a month, with 200GB, shareable with up to five other family members. Both include Apple Music, Apple TV and Apple Arcade. Apple Music is not included in the newly announced iCloud+ bundle, a key distinction for users comparing the offerings.The shift turns cloud storage, often bought when free space runs out, into an entry point for Apple’s entertainment services. For existing iCloud+ customers, the immediate benefit is access to streaming and games without an additional subscription bill.For Apple, bundling could help expose more paying customers to services they may not have chosen separately. It also gives users another reason to retain their storage subscription. However, customers who want only Apple TV or Arcade will now have to take the combined offering when subscribing directly through Apple.“We’re excited to bring Apple TV and Apple Arcade to iCloud+ users in over 100 countries in one convenient subscription,” said Eddy Cue, Apple’s senior vice president of Services and Health.Airtel customers with iPhones can also access the expanded subscription through eligible postpaid plans. Those already receiving Apple TV through select Airtel plans can transition at no additional cost. Availability of individual features, shows and games may vary by country, region or device.Get the latest technology news and updates. Download the TOI App.

articles.title: In 1998, 31 Przewalski’s horses were brought to Chernobyl; deaths and poaching followed before their numbers reached 137 by 2018
articles.summary: Rest of World News: When the Chernobyl Exclusion Zone was abandoned after the 1986 nuclear disaster, it was not expected to become part of the future of a horse that had .
articles.body: When the Chernobyl Exclusion Zone was abandoned after the 1986 nuclear disaster, it was not expected to become part of the future of a horse that had already vanished from the wild. Yet, more than a decade later, Przewalski’s horses were brought into the largely empty landscape in an effort to establish a free-ranging population. According to the study published in Theriologia Ukrainica, titled ‘Przewalski`s horse (Equus ferus przewalskii) in the Chornobyl Exclusion Zone after 20 years of introduction’ claim that 31 horses were released in 1998 and multiplied. The records tell a more complicated story. The animals arrived over two years, some died before joining the wild population, and poaching caused serious losses during the first decade. Even so, the horses continued breeding. By 2018, 137 had been documented in Ukraine, with others across the Belarusian border.How Przewalski’s horses were introduced to the Chernobyl Exclusion ZoneThe introduction began in 1998 and continued into 1999. Twenty-eight Przewalski’s horses came from the Askania Nova Biosphere Reserve, made up of 10 males and 18 females. Three more males were brought from the zoo at the Lozovski stud-farm.That is the origin of the familiar total of 31, although saying that all 31 became the founders of Chernobyl's free-ranging population leaves out what happened next, as reported by Chernobyl, Pripyat, Chernobyl Exclusion Zone.Eight animals died during transport or shortly afterwards, with injury and stress among the recorded problems. Those that survived were not immediately turned loose. They spent anything from several weeks to eight months in large enclosures while they acclimatised.When the early history of the population was later examined, the animals identified as successful reproductive founders were a much smaller group: two stallions and 15 mares from Askania Nova. The purpose of the project was also broader than simply putting an endangered animal into an abandoned radioactive area. The plan was to create a free-ranging population while increasing biodiversity and helping restore ecological processes in a landscape that had been heavily altered by human activity before the disaster.The uncertain history behind Przewalski’s horsesPrzewalski’s horses had disappeared from the wild during the twentieth century. Their survival depended on captive breeding programmes, from which later reintroduction projects were developed.The species has often been described as the world's last truly wild horse, sometimes with the added claim that it was never domesticated. That description has become less straightforward as archaeological evidence has been re-examined.A reassessment published in Scientific Reports in 2021, titled 'Rethinking the evidence for early horse domestication at Botai’ looked again at evidence from Botai in Kazakhstan, a site long associated with early horse domestication. The authors argued that the remains could instead reflect large-scale hunting of wild Przewalski’s horses. Their interpretation did not settle every question about the species' past relationship with people, but it made the old certainty harder to maintain. For Chernobyl, the more immediate fact was simpler. A horse that had survived only through captive populations was being given space to live and breed freely again.Przewalski’s horses grew in number but faced early lossesOnce breeding began, numbers increased quickly. The population reached 65 animals in both 2003 and 2004. That growth did not continue without interruption. By 2007, the number had fallen to around 50. At the end of the following year, 64 horses were counted.Illegal hunting was part of the problem, although the surviving records do not allow every loss to be assigned a cause. Between 1999 and 2006, 55 free-ranging horses were lost. A cause of death could only be determined in 18 cases, and 13 of those deaths were attributed to poaching.The early study therefore found that poaching accounted for more than 70 per cent of the deaths for which a cause was known. It could not say the same about all 55 losses. The horses were reproducing and establishing themselves, but the population was also vulnerable to pressures that could not always be measured clearly from the available records.Chernobyl’s Przewalski’s horses were no longer just scattered survivorsA more detailed picture emerged from camera-trap work carried out in 2018. In the Ukrainian part of the exclusion zone, 137 Przewalski’s horses were recorded. According to the Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations, the count included 47 stallions, 66 adult mares and fillies, and 24 foals. Beyond the Ukrainian survey area, at least four more animals were recorded at a remote site in the Belarusian exclusion zone: one stallion, two mares and a foal.These were not simply scattered individuals moving randomly through the landscape. The survey recorded 13 harem groups containing foals, along with four small groups that were not breeding, around six groups of stallions and at least one solitary male.Some of the horses were using territory on both sides of the international border.Their presence in Belarus had developed over several years. Horses were reported crossing the Prypiat River between 2007 and 2010, after which a breeding subpopulation became established there. By the time of the 2018 survey, the original introduction was already becoming part of the population's distant history. Almost every horse recorded belonged to the second generation or a later one. Only two mares still carried brands linking them directly to the animals brought into the zone at the end of the 1990s.Chernobyl’s wild horses adapted to a landscape far beyond open meadowsPrzewalski’s horses are usually associated with open country, and meadows remained an important part of their habitat in Chernobyl. The 2018 survey, though, showed that the animals were not avoiding forested areas. That is significant because the exclusion zone is far from an open grassland. Woodland and reforested ground cover large areas, and the changing landscape has also made it harder to count animals by direct observation.The horses were using a broader range of habitat than a simple steppe image might suggest. Their movements through forests also help explain why camera traps and repeated field observations became important for understanding how the population was distributed.Population growth cannot answer every question about radiationThe presence of a growing Przewalski’s horse population in Chernobyl does not mean that radiation has no biological effects. Population numbers and the health of individual animals are different questions. A population can grow while some animals experience effects that are not visible in a basic count. At the same time, many pressures disappeared or were greatly reduced when people left the area after the disaster.Farming, traffic, development and regular human disturbance were no longer shaping the landscape in the same way. Those changes created conditions that cannot easily be separated from radiation exposure when looking only at the population's overall increase.The 2018 work was concerned with where the horses lived, how they were organised socially and how the population had developed over time. It was not a controlled experiment designed to isolate radiation as a single variable.Its results show that the horses reproduced successfully and remained established in the exclusion zone. They do not establish that radiation is harmless, nor do they identify one factor as the explanation for the population's survival.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: From TVs to refrigerators: What Amazon's survey reveals about how India shops for appliances
articles.summary: Tech News News: Amazon India has released the third set of findings from its inaugural Best in Tech Survey, revealing how Indian consumers choose Smart TVs and home a.
articles.body: Amazon India has released the third set of findings from its inaugural Best in Tech Survey, revealing how Indian consumers choose Smart TVs and home appliances. Picture quality emerged as the leading feature preference for Smart TV buyers, while energy star rating ranked highest for air conditioner and refrigerator buyers. Flexible financing also plays a decisive role, with nearly half of large appliance buyers citing No-Cost EMI as the most important pricing lever.A data-driven look at what India wantsThe survey, drawn from more than 40,000 responses across major consumer electronics categories, is part of an ongoing Amazon India initiative to understand what shapes tech purchase decisions on its platform. This latest release covers Smart TVs, air conditioners, refrigerators, and washing machines, and its findings will help shape both product selection on Amazon.in and the upcoming second edition of the Best in Tech Awards, scheduled for September 18, 2026.Zeba Khan, Director of Consumer Electronics at Amazon India, said the findings reinforce a pattern seen in the survey's earlier rounds on personal devices, now extending into home appliances as well: brand trust remains foundational, but customers are researching extensively and expecting a consistently high standard across the entire buying journey, from product page to installation. She noted that AI has moved well beyond smartphones and laptops and is now becoming a meaningful part of how people think about home appliances too.Smart TVs: Picture quality rules, AI interest varies by budgetPicture quality emerged as the single most important purchase factor for Smart TV buyers, cited by 66% of respondents. At higher price points above ₹60,000, buyers are gravitating toward OLED and Mini LED/Neo QLED panels, with Mini LED emerging as a strong contender at the premium end. Financing also plays a major role: two-thirds of buyers said EMI or "buy now, pay later" options influence their decision, with EMI mattering to 36% of buyers under Rs 25,000, 40% in the Rs 25,000–Rs 60,000 range, and 38% above that threshold.Preference for premium display technology has also become remarkably consistent nationwide, with roughly 8 in 10 buyers favoring QLED, OLED, or Mini LED/Neo QLED panels across metros as well as Tier 2 and Tier 3 cities, leaving basic LED TVs a small minority almost everywhere.AI-powered features are generating real excitement, with 60% of Smart TV buyers saying they're drawn to them — though what "AI" means to buyers shifts with budget.Buyers spending above ₹60,000 are mainly interested in AI-powered picture enhancement, cited by 51% of premium buyers, while those under ₹25,000 lean toward voice assistants, cited by 39% in that segment. Movies and OTT content remain the top overall reason to buy a Smart TV, followed by family entertainment, while gaming shows particular strength in Tier 2 cities. Installation also directly shapes purchase decisions for over a third of buyers, reflecting an expectation that the experience doesn't end at checkout.Air conditioners: Energy efficiency and transparent installation matter mostFor AC buyers, a high energy star rating is the top priority, cited by 35% of respondents, ahead of inverter technology (24%) and convertible cooling (21%) — suggesting energy efficiency itself, rather than the specific underlying technology, has become the primary filter buyers apply. On the service side, nearly half of AC buyers said free installation with no hidden charges is their top expectation, followed by trained and certified technicians (20%) and combined delivery-and-installation in a single visit (17%).Refrigerators: Delivery experience is the deciding factorRefrigerator buyers put an unusually strong emphasis on delivery quality: seven in ten said damage-free delivery with full packaging inspection is their top expectation, well ahead of old-refrigerator exchange or removal (16%) and exact placement within the kitchen (9%). On the product side, energy star rating again topped the list of desired features at 30%, followed by convertible modes (25%) and inverter compressors (22%). When it comes to what would justify spending beyond a planned budget, 28% pointed to a significantly higher energy rating with provable long-term savings, another 28% cited genuinely useful convertible technology, and 18% said longer warranty periods would justify paying more.Washing machines: Inverter motors lead, AI wash programs gaining groundWashing machine buyers ranked inverter motors as their top feature, cited by 40% of respondents for their combination of quiet operation, energy savings, and durability. AI-powered wash programs that automatically detect fabric type and load size are emerging as a fast-rising second choice at 18%, suggesting smart laundry features are shifting from a premium extra to a mainstream expectation. Nearly half of buyers said delivery and installation need to happen in a single visit, with professional plumbing setup the second most commonly cited need at 20%.This installment builds on two earlier rounds of the Best in Tech Survey. The first found that AI features now influence purchase decisions for 82% of smartphone buyers on Amazon.in, while the second found processor performance to be the top driver for laptop buyers at 87%, with AI enthusiasm running highest in the computing category. Across all three rounds, a consistent theme has emerged: Indian buyers are evaluating tech and appliance purchases on detailed specifications, prioritizing efficiency and long-term value, and expecting the post-purchase experience — delivery, installation, and setup — to match the quality of the product itself.Get the latest technology news and updates. articles.title: Does India still need Russia’s S-500? How its own missile shield is changing the equation
articles.summary: News News: Recent and ongoing conflicts have demonstrated the requirement for a comprehensive and layered air defence environment. Modern air defences are tasked.
articles.body: Recent and ongoing conflicts have demonstrated the requirement for a comprehensive and layered air defence environment. Modern air defences are tasked with defending against everything from the off the shelf drone to ballistic missiles and everything in between. During the active phase of Operation Sindoor, India defended against almost the entire spectrum of aerial threats ranging from small Pakistani drones to ballistic missiles. Even, well over a year, the Pakistanis have not been able to provide proof of their strikes, instead resorting to AI generated videos on their National Defence Day earlier this month.During the active phase of the operation in May last year, the Pakistanis fired a Fatah series of ballistic missile that wad intercepted over Sirsa in Haryana by the air force. Hunting ballistic missiles is one of the most complex tasks and requires the precise working of different types of systems ranging from the early warning radar to the acquisition radar that relays information to the firing unit and at the end the interceptor that has to connect with a projectile hurtling towards the earth at hypersonic speeds. The devastation caused by these weapons has been on display with the Iranians and their proxies the Houthis terrorising the region with these weapons.To tackle this problem, the Russians have developed the S-500 Prometheus system. This weapons complex armed with missiles such as the 77N6 and a variant of this missile named the 77N6-N1 which can take out ballistic missiles at ranges of up to 600 km at altitudes of up to 200 km. According to Washington DC based think tank, the Center for Strategic and International Studies (CSIS), this missile is also capable of taking out Low Earth Orbit (LEO) satellites. Unlike the S-400, which offers theatre-level protection out to 400 kilometres against aircraft, drones and cruise missiles, the S-500 Prometheus is not designed to replace the S-400, but to supplement it. With the S-400 being more adept at taking down aircraft, drones and cruise missiles, this leaves open other threats such as ballistic missiles and hypersonic weapons. The Russians have been pitching the S-500 to India since 2021.This comes at a time when India is developing its own Ballistic Missile Defence (BMD) apparatus. The country has taken a major leap in its missile defence capability, successfully completing the final development trials of Phase-II of its Ballistic Missile Defence shield. Conducted by DRDO on June 10-11 using the AD-1 and AD-2 interceptors, the tests validated India's ability to intercept incoming ballistic missiles both inside and outside the atmosphere, placing the country in a select group of nations capable of defending against ICBM-class threats.The system is designed to counter some of the most challenging targets in modern warfare, hypersonic weapons, manoeuvring glide vehicles, and missiles fitted with MIRV technology that can release multiple warheads toward different targets simultaneously. This layered shield relies on a network of launch vehicles, long-range radars, Launch Control Centres and a central Mission Control Centre, all linked through a secure communication system.While Phase-I already offers limited operational protection to Delhi and Mumbai against threats up to 2,000 kilometres, Phase-II extends that umbrella dramatically, to missiles with ranges approaching 5,000 kilometres. Defence Minister Rajnath Singh described the tests as validating the critical technologies underpinning India's broader multi-layered defence shield.Mobility is central to the new system too, with indigenous 12x12 Transporter-Erector-Launchers, built by Ashok Leyland and integrated by DRDO and Tata Advanced Systems, giving the AD-1 and AD-2 interceptors genuine shoot-and-scoot capability across difficult terrain. With the domestic BMD system maturing under the overall ambit of Project Kusha, the space for a foreign weapons project could perhaps be reducing.

articles.title: 'Distressing': BJP slams Congress over three of its CMs 'skipping' Brics dinner
articles.summary: India News: NEW DELHI: Bharatiya Janata Party on Tuesday slammed Congress after three of its chief ministers skipped the dinner for Brics leaders hosted by the go.

articles.title: In the 1940s, common ragweed spread with American agricultural aid meant to rebuild Japan, but it became widespread across roadsides, fields, and cities nationwide and contributed to seasonal hay fever
articles.summary: Rest of World News: Explore the unexpected arrival of common ragweed in Japan post-World War II, its spread across the nation, and its significant impact on public health, triggering a hay fever epidemic that persists to this day.
articles.body: Massive amounts of food, seed, and raw materials must be transported across borders to rebuild a nation following a catastrophic conflict, typically with significantly more hurry than caution. The United States provided Japan with this kind of extensive assistance in the years following World War II in the form of wheat, animal feed, and other agricultural supplies meant to avert widespread hunger and revive Japanese agriculture. Among the plants that later benefited from increased movement of agricultural goods was common ragweed, Ambrosia artemisiifolia, a North American species capable of thriving in disturbed ground. Japan's experience would eventually turn the plant from a minor introduction into a widespread source of seasonal pollen.An old arrival that spread after conditions changedCommon ragweed had reached Japan decades before the war, with the first record dating to around 1877. Japan's National Institute for Environmental Studies lists the species as an introduced plant that later established itself in the wild. For decades, it remained a relatively limited introduction rather than a nationwide presence.What changed after 1945 was the scale of disturbance and the movement of goods. Bomb-damaged urban areas, cleared building sites, expanding farmland and newly disturbed roadsides created the kind of open ground on which ragweed could thrive. Increased movement of agricultural commodities also provided opportunities for seeds to travel. The species eventually became widespread across Japan, occurring in farmland, orchards, pastures, roadsides, vacant lots, woodland edges and riverbanks.From nuisance on the roadside to established allergiesJapan's recognition of pollen allergy developed gradually. A systematic study of pollinosis carried out in 1960–61 included a patient with ragweed pollinosis, providing an early documented example of pollen-related allergy in the country. Japanese cedar pollinosis was identified separately after doctors in Nikko investigated patients with recurring spring symptoms in 1963, with the first report published in 1964.Cedar and cypress pollen dominate Japan's spring allergy season, while ragweed releases its pollen in late summer and early autumn, creating a later period of seasonal exposure, which releases its pollen in late summer and early fall, providing Japan a second, lesser wave of seasonal allergy sufferers each year. In urban Saitama, airborne pollen surveys found ragweed pollen levels exceeded the level associated with the onset of clinical allergy symptoms for approximately six weeks in early autumn, and on some days pollen levels were so high that they posed a risk of triggering asthma-related emergency visits.A plant no one has learnt to weed outCommon ragweed remains widespread in Japan and is recognized as an invasive alien species. The National Institute for Environmental Studies lists competition with native plants among its ecological effects, while the species is also important from a public-health perspective because its pollen can trigger seasonal allergic reactions.Research on common ragweed in other regions has similarly linked its spread to international grain trade and transportation networks. A recent study of East China, for example, identified multiple introductions and found that modern grain trade between the United States and China was a major invasion pathway. Ragweed can spread through trade and transportation before becoming established in disturbed habitats. Japan's history with the plant illustrates how an introduction recorded in the 19th century can expand over subsequent decades and eventually become both an ecological and public-health concern. Japan’s postwar experience, driven by an emergency to feed the population, left it with a seasonal health annoyance that outlasted the crisis that birthed it by many decades.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: In 1930, St Kilda’s last residents evacuated the Scottish islands; within 18 months, its house mice vanished while larger field mice moved into abandoned homes
articles.summary: Rest of World News: In 1930, the evacuation of human residents from Scotland’s St Kilda islands led to the extinction of the St Kilda house mouse while the field mouse thrived in the abandoned habitats. This article explores the ecological impact of human departure and the fate of two mouse populations.
articles.body: The last residents of St Kilda left the remote Scottish archipelago in 1930, bringing an end to a human community that had survived on the islands for generations. The departure’s impact went far beyond the social history of the isolated settlement. Within around 18 months, the St Kilda house mouse, a population that was closely associated with human habitation, became extinct. On the other hand, the islands’ already-established field mice expanded into abandoned buildings that were previously occupied almost exclusively by house mice.About 66 kilometres west of Benbecula in Scotland’s Outer Hebrides lies St Kilda. Its largest island, Hirta, was the centre of the permanent settlement, and by the beginning of 1930, only 36 people remained there, according to the National Records of Scotland. They lived in 10 households, while six of the island’s 16 rented cottages were already empty. Sheep rearing, fishing and the harvesting of seabird resources, which were considered traditional livelihoods, had become increasingly difficult to sustain. In addition to this, sometimes bad weather would interrupt deliveries of food and mail.The evacuation that followed was therefore not a part of a response to an ecological experiment. Instead, after a particularly difficult winter in 1929–30, the remaining residents decided that staying on the island was no longer viable. Archived records suggest that the residents requested evacuation, and that on 29 August 1930 the remaining community left for the Scottish mainland. This departure unintentionally impacted the conditions under which two different mouse populations had lived alongside one another.With the departure of humans, house mice lost their human-made habitatSt Kilda had two distinctive mouse populations. One was the St Kilda house mouse, Mus musculus muralis, a form of mouse associated with the island’s human settlement, and the other was the St Kilda field mouse, Apodemus sylvaticus hirtensis, a subspecies of wood mouse that survived in the island’s natural environment. Despite being island forms, both populations’ relationships with human habitation were different. According to the National Trust for Scotland, the St Kilda house mouse became extinct after the 1930 evacuation, while the field mouse remains common on Hirta and is also found on Dun.Conditions created by a permanent human population had greatly benefited the house mice. The houses provided shelter, while food stored by the humans offered a dependable resource for them. On the other hand, field mice were already established on the island but were less closely associated with human buildings. Therefore, when people disappeared from the island, the change was not that a new species suddenly arrived. Instead, the balance between the two populations changed drastically because one species lost the environment they were habituated to.In the summer of 1931, T.H. Harrisson and J.A. Moy-Thomas visited St Kilda and reported in January 1932’s Nature publication that the house mouse had become extremely rare. They found it in only two of the recently vacated households where perishable food supplies had been left behind during the final 1930 evacuation. The 1931 visit indicated that some house mice were still surviving less than a year after the evacuation, especially in places where food remained. Published in the Journal of Zoology in 1969, a later assessment by R.J. Berry and B.J.K. Tricker concluded that the St Kilda house mouse became extinct within 18 months of the human population leaving in 1930.An early explanation for the extinction suggested that mice could no longer obtain enough food after the islanders left; but Berry and Tricker argued that competition with the field mouse was a more likely explanation. They suggested that the mere absence of humans was not sufficient to explain their extinction, as house mice can survive on uninhabited islands. The human departure, instead, stripped the house mice off their structural advantage, thus triggering a lethal survival competition that the wild field mice eventually won.The mouse population that was already established on St KildaThe disappearance of the human population in 1930 changed the field mouse’s relationship with the village buildings. The researchers suggested that the disappearance allowed the field mouse to enter a habitat that had previously been dominated by the house mouse.Apodemus sylvaticus hirtensis is a distinct St Kilda subspecies of the wood mouse and is larger than mainland forms. In a 1969 study of Apodemus sylvaticus populations across the Hebrides and Shetland, Berry argued that most of the island forms were unlikely remnants of prehistoric populations and were more probably introduced by humans. He suggested that Vikings or their descendants were the most likely agents.This is, however, a historical evolutionary interpretation rather than a documented record of exactly when the St Kilda population arrived. Today, the field mouse remains part of St Kilda’s ecosystem. As per the National Trust for Scotland, it is still common in Hirta and is also present on Dun, where it reportedly feeds on snails, insects, moss and seeds.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Nato jets shoot down drone in Lithuanian airspace after Rutte warns Russia against strikes near alliance territory
articles.summary: Europe News: NEW DELHI: Nato fighter jets shot down a drone that entered Lithuanian airspace overnight, officials said Tuesday, in an incident that came less than .
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Nato fighter jets shot down a drone that entered Lithuanian airspace overnight, officials said Tuesday, in an incident that came less than a day after Nato Secretary-General Mark Rutte warned that strikes close to alliance territory would push the bloc to step up support for Ukraine.The drone was shot down near the village of Pratkūnai in the Kaišiadorys district, about 100 km west of Vilnius and near the Kaunas Reservoir, Lithuania’s National Crisis Management Center said.Lithuania’s military said it was the first time a drone had been shot down in the country’s airspace. Authorities did not disclose the drone’s origin or purpose, saying the incident remains under investigation.The incursion came shortly after Rutte, speaking at Nato headquarters in Brussels on Monday, said strikes “close to NATO territory” demonstrated Russian President Vladimir Putin’s “desperation and also his desire to sow fear and terror.”“Russia is growing increasingly reckless as it continues its terrible war against Ukraine,” Rutte said. He also pledged to strengthen the 32-member alliance’s defences along its eastern border with Russia.Drone ‘likely’ carrying explosivesDrone incursions have repeatedly raised security concerns in Lithuania, which borders Belarus, a close Russian ally, and Russia’s Kaliningrad exclave.Antanas Matutis, commander of the Lithuanian air force, said wreckage from the drone had been recovered and that it “likely” was carrying explosives.Vilmantas Vitkauskas, head of Lithuania’s crisis management centre, told public broadcaster LRT that the drone most likely entered Lithuanian airspace from Belarus. It remained in the country for about 30 minutes and flew along the outskirts of populated areas before being intercepted, he said.Kyiv says it is ‘ready to support de-escalation’The incident came as Russian drone strikes continued across Ukraine, following a social media post by US President Donald Trump on Monday claiming Russia and Ukraine had agreed “not to hit” each other’s energy infrastructure.Trump provided no further details about the purported agreement, while Russia did not immediately comment. Previous attempts to broker even limited ceasefires have repeatedly collapsed, with Moscow and Kyiv accusing each other of violations.Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said late Monday that Kyiv was “ready to support de-escalation.”“We see that the Russians feel the pressure from our precise strikes on Russia’s war economy. And so far, no one has seen any genuine desire on Russia’s part to move toward ending the war,” he said. “But if our American partners can ensure that Russia is genuinely ready to stop this war aimed at destroying life — and to do so for real and for the long term — Ukraine will take its own de-escalatory steps.”Ukraine’s State Emergency Service said Tuesday that eight people were wounded in Russian strikes on Kyiv since the start of the day, including two people injured in strikes on gas stations in the capital.Meanwhile, Russia’s Defence Ministry said its forces shot down 222 Ukrainian drones overnight.In the Russian city of Taganrog, a “massive” Ukrainian drone attack sparked several fires, regional Governor Yuri Slyusar said. He said two apartment buildings and three private homes were damaged, along with an educational institution, agricultural warehouses and a site belonging to Russian e-commerce company Ozon.Catch the latest World News and Live updates.
